postings.title: Associate Partner Manager
postings.location: Atlanta, Georgia, United States of America
postings.description:
At Liberis, our mission is to empower small and medium-sized businesses by removing finance as a friction to growth, delivering contextual, embedded financial solutions to support merchants at every stage of their business lifecycle.

The Role

As an Associate Partner Manager, you’ll help manage and grow our embedded finance partnerships, combining relationship building, commercial awareness and hands-on coordination to deliver a great experience for our partners and their merchants.

You’ll take day-to-day responsibility for a portfolio of partners, managing strategy, complex issues and expansion opportunities. Working closely with partners and internal teams, you’ll help strengthen merchant engagement, improve performance and keep initiatives moving.

This is an opportunity to further build your experience in fintech partnerships while making a direct contribution to commercial growth across the merchant lifecycle.

What you’ll be doing

- Build partner relationships: Act as a day-to-day contact for your partners, building strong working relationships and keeping communication clear and consistent. Prepare for business reviews, contribute to performance discussions and follow through on agreed actions.

- Support commercial growth: Work with partners and internal teams to improve marketing activity, lead generation and the merchant experience. Help deliver revenue targets by increasing merchant adoption, product take-up, renewals and retention.

- Spot opportunities to grow: Use partner conversations and performance data to identify opportunities for new products or merchant segments. Gather requirements and work with senior colleagues to assess and develop these opportunities.

- Keep initiatives moving: Coordinate with Product, Partner Solutions and other teams on launches and improvements. Track actions, owners and timelines, flagging risks and dependencies early.

- Maintain operational quality: Monitor partner performance and the merchant journey, helping identify issues with data, integrations or application flows. Work with Operations, Underwriting and Risk to resolve problems and escalate where needed.

- Help partners succeed: Support joint campaigns, merchant education and partner training alongside Marketing and other teams. Help partner sales and customer success teams understand our products and use reporting tools effectively.

- Turn data into action: Maintain accurate partner reporting and track conversion, product adoption and renewals. Identify trends, share practical recommendations and follow up on actions to improve performance.

What we think you’ll need

- Around 2–4 years of relevant experience in partnerships, account management, customer success or a similar commercially focused role.

- Experience fintech and embedded finance, exposure to payments or lending would be helpful.

- Experience building B2B relationships and taking responsibility for day-to-day account activity.

- Commercial awareness and an interest in understanding what drives partner performance and growth.

- Confidence working with data and spreadsheets to track results, identify trends and recommend next steps.

- Strong organisation and follow-through, with the ability to coordinate several priorities across different teams.

- Clear communication and relationship-building skills, including confidence asking questions and raising issues.

- A proactive, hands-on approach and the ability to work at pace as priorities change.

- A willingness to learn about lending workflows, partner integrations and the merchant lifecycle.

What happens next?

Think this sounds like the right next move for you? Or if you’re not completely confident that you fit our exact criteria, apply anyway and we can arrange a call to see if the role is fit for you. Humility is a wonderful thing, and we are interested in hearing about what you can add to Liberis!

The team

We are the Collections team! A dedicated group with a clear mission: to assist customers facing financial challenges and guide them back to good standing wherever possible. With team members based in the UK, Sweden, Germany and the US, we are looking for an enthusiastic Collections Agent to join our rapidly growing global Collections team and support Liberis' growth in the German and Czech/Slovak markets!

As a Collections Agent, you'll take the helm in our in-house collection process, steering a diverse receivables book toward success. Your mission: to maintain impeccable standards of accuracy and timeliness, driving up collection rates while ensuring every customer enjoys a top-notch experience.

postings.title: Director of Business Development, Enterprise Partnerships
postings.location: Atlanta, Georgia, United States of America
postings.description:
At Liberis, our mission is to empower small and medium-sized businesses by removing finance as a friction to growth, delivering contextual, embedded financial solutions to support merchants at every stage of their business lifecycle.

The team 

The Business Development team identifies and secures new enterprise partnerships that drive Liberis' growth. We work with marketplaces, eCommerce platforms, ISVs, payment providers and logistics networks to build compelling propositions, agree sustainable commercial terms and lay the foundations for successful launches. 

We work closely with colleagues across Commercial, Product, Technology, Operations, Finance, Legal and Risk to turn opportunities into commercially valuable partnerships. 

The role 

We are looking for a Director of Business Development to originate and close enterprise embedded finance partnerships, owning some of our largest and most complex opportunities across marketplaces, eCommerce, ISVs, payments and shipping/logistics. 

You will build a strong pipeline and convert it into partnerships that deliver sustainable, profitable growth. You will draw on your existing network and track record of launching embedded lending, banking and payments programs to open doors with senior decision-makers, shape where we focus and lead complex negotiations through to signed agreement. 

This is a senior individual contributor role. You will work closely with a Business Development Manager to manage deals from first meeting through to launch, combining strategic judgement with hands-on ownership of deals, working independently and bringing colleagues together to build compelling propositions and secure successful outcomes. 

Your responsibilities 

- Identify and prioritise strategic embedded finance opportunities across partner types (marketplaces, eCommerce platforms, ISVs, payment providers, shipping and logistics), verticals and markets. 

- Build and manage your own pipeline, with accountability for acquisition targets and the commercial value of new agreements. 

- Personally originate and lead major enterprise opportunities, from initial engagement through to signed agreement, tapping your existing network of senior contacts. 

- Build trusted relationships with executive stakeholders and navigate complex partner organisations, including product, payments, risk, legal and finance teams. 

- Shape partnership propositions for embedded lending, banking and payments that address partner priorities, meet merchant needs and create attractive economics for Liberis. 

- Develop high-quality presentations, proposals and commercial models that support partner decisions. 

- Lead commercial negotiations, balancing growth potential, profitability, delivery requirements and risk. 

- Secure internal alignment for opportunities, present clear business cases and resolve barriers to progress. 

- Maintain reliable forecasts and give senior leadership a clear view of deal progress, key decisions and risks. 

- Work with implementation and partner management teams to ensure agreed commitments are achievable and partnerships are set up to deliver. 

- Bring market and partner insight into decisions on product development, competitive positioning and expansion. 

- Contribute to best practice across Business Development through your experience, insight and approach to complex deals. 

- Represent Liberis at industry events and develop relationships that create new commercial opportunities. 

What we are looking for 

Experience 

- 10 or more years in enterprise sales, business development or strategic partnerships, with a significant portion selling embedded lending, banking or payments solutions to enterprise platforms. 

- A proven record of originating and closing embedded finance programs: signed clients or partnerships you have personally secured, with measurable commercial results. 

- A strong track record of personally securing substantial B2B partnerships involving complex negotiations and multiple decision-makers. 

- Experience independently managing long enterprise deal cycles, from origination through to commercial agreement and launch. 

Network and market knowledge 

- An established network of senior contacts across marketplaces, eCommerce platforms, ISVs, payment providers (PSPs, acquirers, processors) and/or shipping and logistics companies, with the ability to open executive-level conversations. 

- A strong understanding of fintech, payments, SaaS and embedded finance, and how platforms monetise and serve small businesses. 

Commercial and influencing skills 

- Confidence assessing commercial models (revenue share, referral and funding economics), challenging assumptions and translating opportunities into credible business cases. 

- Experience influencing senior stakeholders internally and externally, including executives at large organisations. 

Nice to have 

- Experience in small business lending, merchant cash advance or revenue-based financing. 

- Familiarity with API and platform integrations, and with the regulatory and risk considerations of offering financial products through a partner. 

And there’s plenty more! Enjoy 25 days’ PTO, competitive healthcare benefits and up to 60 days per year working from anywhere. Apply to discover the full benefits package and what life at Liberis has to offer.

Think this sounds like the right next move for you? Or if you’re not completely confident that you fit our exact criteria, apply anyway and we can arrange a call to see if the role is fit for you. Humility is a wonderful thing, and we are interested in hearing about what you can add to Liberis!

postings.title: Director of Partnerships - UK
postings.description:
At Liberis, our mission is to empower small and medium-sized businesses by removing finance as a friction to growth, delivering contextual, embedded financial solutions to support merchants at every stage of their business lifecycle.

The Role

The Director of Partnerships - UK leads our UK partnerships end to end: the team of Partner Managers who run day-to-day relationships, the senior relationships and negotiations that shape each partner’s future with Liberis, and the growth plan that turns those relationships into funding volume and revenue.

This is a broader role than a team lead. You will combine people leadership with commercial ownership: deepening our existing UK partnerships and expanding the products and segments we offer through each. You will lead a team of Partner Managers (currently four) and, as we move to a regional operating model from January 2027, shape how the team is organised around partner growth and partner needs.

Managing senior relationships is the heart of this role. You will be the trusted counterpart of our UK partners at executive and senior leadership level and own the relationships that matter most. You will connect each partner’s strategy and operating model to Liberis’ goals, products and priorities, so that we run growing, profitable partnership programs and defend and retain our market position against competition.

Our UK partners span four partner types: merchant acquirers, ISOs, marketplaces and payment providers. Each has its own commercial model, decision-makers and way of working with us.

What you'll be doing

Own and lead senior partner relationships

- Own the most senior relationships at our UK partners (merchant acquirers, ISOs, marketplaces and payment providers) at executive and senior leadership level, for example C-suite, Managing Director, VP and Head of function across Commercial, Product, Data, Risk and Operations.

- Be the accountable owner of each partner’s long-term future with Liberis and the escalation point for senior stakeholders on both sides.

- Understand each partner’s strategy, operating model and what they are optimising for, and connect the dots between that and what Liberis can offer.

- Set the agenda, roadmap and priorities with each partner, balancing their needs against Liberis’ goals, objectives, product offering and prioritisation.

- Lead commercial and contract negotiations at this level, including pricing, commission, exclusivity and data-access terms, together with Legal and Finance.

- Run executive-level governance with partner leadership: QBRs, annual planning and strategy sessions.

- Make sure relationships are multi-threaded across each partner, so that no key relationship depends on a single person.

- Represent Liberis as a trusted advisor on embedded finance best practice.

- Defend and retain our position with partners against competitors, and know when and how to respond to competitive moves.

Lead the UK Partnerships team

- Lead, coach and develop a team of Partner Managers (currently four), setting clear expectations, standards and ways of working.

- Coach your team to prepare for and hold senior conversations, and step in where a relationship needs your level.

- Own hiring, capability building and succession for the team, and build a culture of ownership and accountability.

- Set the governance rhythm (MBRs, QBRs, roadmap reviews) and make sure it is consistent, insight-led and drives action.

- Act as the escalation point for key partners and internal teams.

Own commercial outcomes

- Own the revenue, funding volume, conversion and unit-economics drivers for the UK partner portfolio, and the plan to deliver them.

- Operate growing and profitable partnership programs, making trade-offs between partner growth and Liberis’ profitability explicit.

- Lead forecasting and commercial planning with Finance and Analytics, and be accountable for accuracy.

- Identify and act on funnel, pricing, renewal and penetration opportunities across the full merchant lifecycle, not just initial originations.

- Assess the commercial viability, operational readiness and P&L impact of proposed expansions and new product launches.

Grow and expand existing partnerships

- Lead partner discussions on new products and new merchant segments.

- Shape the proposition for each partner and align it with Product and Solutions on scope, integration and launch.

- Take on newly signed partners from BD and make sure they launch and ramp well.

Work across the business and across regions

- Work with Product, Partner Solutions, Underwriting, Risk, Marketing and Operations to deliver launches and lifecycle improvements.

- Make sure partner priorities, risks, dependencies and roadmap commitments are aligned internally.

- Work closely with the Director of Partnerships, UK/EU, who also owns our EU partners, so that partners operating in both UK and EU are managed under one plan and one voice.

- Partner with the Global Partnerships team on globally owned partners, shared standards and reporting, and bring UK insight into the global agenda.

- Support multi-market opportunities with the EU team, for example marketplace and platform partners that operate across the UK and EU.

What you’ll need

Must have

- Proven experience in partnerships or Key Account Management, including leading a team of partner- or Key Account facing managers.

- Commercially minded: you have owned revenue, P&L drivers or commercial outcomes, and can show the results.

- Familiarity with embedded finance, in either lending or payments.

- Experience building and negotiating relationships at executive and senior leadership level (e.g. C-suite, Managing Director, VP, Head of function), including contract negotiations.

- Ability to own the most senior partner relationships and read a partner’s strategy and operating model to align it with Liberis’ goals, product offerings and priorities.

- Experience with partner types such as merchant acquirers, ISOs, marketplaces or payment providers.

Also valued

- Experience managing complex B2B2B or B2B2C partnerships and platform ecosystems.

- Analytical skills with funnel data, renewals and financial metrics.

- Understanding of lending workflows, underwriting concepts and partner integrations.

- A track record of building and developing teams.

Our hybrid approach

Working together in person helps us move faster, collaborate better, and build a great Liberis culture. This role requires at least three days per week in the office, with flexibility around which days depending on team and business needs. Our ways of working may evolve over time, including office attendance expectations. At Liberis, we embrace flexibility as a core part of our culture, while also valuing the importance of the time our teams spend together in the office.

Who are we

The finance team is at the heart of Liberis operations. Our mission is to support the future growth of the company by:

- Providing insightful financial information to management and investors

- Developing a scalable finance platform capable of ensuring proper oversight and compliance

We are currently a team of sixteen based in London and Mumbai with responsibility for partnering with our Global operational teams. You’ll join a dynamic, fast paced innovative team, made up of enthusiastic and experienced finance professionals. You’ll help us drive business performance by continually challenging our ways of working, developing a best-in-class financial process while ensuring compliance with all global reporting and tax requirements.

Who are you?

You are a qualified accountant who is keen to work in a rapidly evolving business – providing business insight and ensuring our standards and compliance are best-in-class. You’ll thrive on process innovation and challenging the status quo to achieve great results.

Responsibilities

- Preparation of the monthly consolidated management accounts, supporting analysis and reporting for the Board and external investors;

- Various analysis of group, subsidiary and branch balances on a monthly basis ensuring robust controls around reporting and reconciliation.

- Ownership of group balance sheet reconciliations, including intercompany balances

- Management of the SAP system to meet the developing needs of the business, maintaining the chart of accounts and other masterdata and managing internal controls;

- Assist with company’s auditors during the interim and yearend review to confirm the transactions and balances reported in the financial statements;

- A qualified Accountant (ACCA, ACA or equivalent) with 2 -5 years’ experience post qualification – we are open to backgrounds both in industry or practice!

- Strong technical knowledge of IFRS and UK GAAP and local tax compliance requirements

- Experience preparing group consolidations, including intercompany eliminations and foreign currency translation.

- Outstanding spreadsheet skills and knowledge of financial reporting systems (preferably SAP or Microsoft Dynamics)

- Experience with AI including ChatGPT and Claude

- A track record of process improvement and innovation

- Demonstrates ambition and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment.

- You will thrive if you are a self-motivated, fast-paced, action oriented, “roll your sleeves up and get-things-done” sort of person who wants to work in a medium size team where everyone makes a difference.

- Roll your sleeves up. You are happy to do the detailed work yourself, from drafting the policy paper to checking the reconciliation.

- Self-directed. You can take a loosely defined problem, work out a plan and deliver it with minimal supervision, and you know when to raise a flag.

- Project minded. You manage your own timelines and keep stakeholders informed without being chased

- Clear communicator. You’ll be translating complex accounting topics to non-accounting audiences.

- Collaborative. You build good working relationships with colleagues in both businesses.

postings.description:

The team

We are responsible for finding and signing Liberis’ partners of the future. We manage opportunities across the full business development lifecycle, from identifying the right prospects through to signing agreements and supporting new partners as they prepare to launch. 

This includes: 

- Identifying and qualifying potential partners 

- Building relationships and leading early-stage conversations 

- Shaping the scope of each partnership and helping define the product and proposition 

- Developing commercial proposals and negotiating partnership agreements 

- Working with teams across Liberis to support onboarding and launch 

The role

Your primary focus will be helping Liberis secure new partnerships. 

This is a varied role with the opportunity to take full ownership of partnership opportunities while contributing to some of our largest and most complex global deals. You will work with prospective partners and colleagues across Commercial, Product, Technology, Operations, Finance, Legal and Risk. 

Your responsibilities will include: 

- Shaping, owning and progressing partnership opportunities from initial conversation through to agreement 

- Researching and qualifying opportunities within the early-stage pipeline 

- Building strong relationships with prospective partners and understanding their priorities 

- Defining the scope, product and commercial proposition for new partnerships 

- Producing high-quality partner materials, including presentations, proposals and commercial models 

- Driving proposals, negotiations and deal cycles for global enterprise opportunities 

- Coordinating internal teams and maintaining momentum throughout the deal process 

- Leading the handover and onboarding of new partners ahead of launch 

- Representing Liberis at relevant industry events and using them to develop new opportunities 

- Contributing to best practice and improving how the Business Development team operates 

What we are looking for 

- You’ll have 3-6 years experience in business development, partnerships or a related commercial role, with some exposure to complex B2B deal cycles. 

- Experience in financial services, fintech, payments or SaaS would be helpful, but isn’t essential. 

- You will bring an ability to learn quickly, exercise good commercial judgement and implement structure to opportunities involving several internal and external stakeholders. 

We think success in the role comes down to four areas: 

- Depth of understanding: You will develop a strong understanding of our products, platform and financial solutions, as well as the markets in which we operate. You should be naturally curious and able to get to grips with new business models and unfamiliar topics quickly. 

- Relationship building: You can build rapport with a wide range of people, both internally and externally. You will be comfortable working across different business functions and communicating with stakeholders at different levels of an organization. 

- Commercial acumen: You have good commercial instincts and can identify what matters in a potential partnership. You can understand different commercial models, contribute to negotiations and balance the needs of Liberis with those of the partner. 

- High-quality execution: You can bring structure to complex and sometimes ambiguous deal cycles. You are organized, reliable and able to manage several workstreams while maintaining attention to detail. 

From a personal perspective, we are looking for someone who: 

- Takes individual accountability and follows through on commitments 

- Is comfortable working in an environment where not every answer is immediately clear 

- Approaches problems in a structured and practical way 

- Is naturally curious and keen to learn

postings.title: Senior Underwriter
postings.description:
At Liberis, our mission is to empower small and medium-sized businesses by removing finance as a friction to growth, delivering contextual, embedded financial solutions to support merchants at every stage of their business lifecycle.

The team

We are the Risk team responsible for managing the credit risk of Liberis’ portfolios, which include designing effective new strategies, managing the credit quality of our products across geographies, and providing specialist credit risk advice to the business.

The Risk team is primarily based in London, UK with colleagues in Atlanta, US and Stockholm, Sweden too and covers Risk Analytics, Decision Science and Underwriting. Our mission is to grow Liberis profitably to become the leading embedded business finance provider and we are looking for an Underwriter to join us on this journey.

Who are you?

You are an experienced underwriter who combines strong credit judgment with a practical, customer-aware approach. You are comfortable making independent decisions on complex applications, explaining your rationale, and helping others strengthen theirs. You take ownership of quality and timeliness and use your experience to improve how the team works.

Reporting to the Senior Underwriting Manager in Atlanta, you will serve as a senior individual contributor within the US Underwriting team. You will assess higher-complexity applications, act as a referral point, coach and mentor for your colleagues, and contribute thought leadership to the continued development of our US underwriting approach.

What you’ll be doing

As a Senior Underwriter, you will combine expert deal assessment with informal leadership across the team. You will make sound, balanced decisions that protect Liberis while helping small businesses access responsible finance.

- Independently assess new and repeat funding applications, using bank statements, credit bureau data, financial statements, and other relevant information to make well-supported decisions

- Exercise delegated approval authority with sound judgment, clearly documenting decision rationale and escalating applications when appropriate

- Serve as a referral and escalation point for underwriters and business stakeholders on complex, unusual, or higher-risk applications

- Coach and mentor underwriters through case discussions, side-by-side reviews, constructive feedback, and regular decision calibration

- Support onboarding and ongoing development by sharing practical underwriting knowledge, strengthening consistency, and modeling high standards

- Partner with customers and internal teams to gather information, resolve questions, and communicate underwriting decisions clearly and professionally

- Provide underwriting thought leadership by identifying portfolio trends, emerging risks, and opportunities to strengthen policies, controls, and decision quality

- Lead or support process improvements and ad-hoc analysis that improve efficiency while maintaining an appropriate balance between customer experience and risk

What we think you’ll need

The best Senior Underwriters can make decisions strategically when information is limited. They combine technical expertise with sound judgment, communicate their reasoning, and raise the capability of the people around them. Our team currently consists of several bright and talented individuals, and our next hire will further strengthen the team by not only contributing to underwriting interesting and complex deals but also by introducing fresh and experienced perspective.

- 5+ years of experience in underwriting, ideally in small-business finance or a similar lending environment

- A strong record of making independent credit decisions on complex applications and defending those decisions with clear, evidence-based reasoning

- Strong knowledge of cash-flow analysis, affordability, financial statements, credit bureau information, fraud indicators, and common small-business debt structures

- Demonstrated experience coaching or mentoring colleagues and giving constructive feedback that improves judgment and performance

- The ability to provide thought leadership, challenge existing approaches constructively, and influence decisions across teams

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex credit decisions to varied audiences

- Sharp attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities, high application volumes, and service-level expectations

- Strong Excel skills; analytical training and exposure to SQL are a plus

What happens next?

Think this sounds like the right next move for you? Or if you’re not completely confident that you fit our exact criteria, apply anyway and we can arrange a call to see if the role is fit for you. Humility is a wonderful thing, and we are interested in hearing about what you can add to Liberis!
